title: Claude Sonnet 5
content:
## Overview

Claude Sonnet 5 launched on **June 30, 2026**, and became the new default model across Claude.ai's Free and Pro plans, with availability for Max, Team, and Enterprise users and full access via the Claude Platform API and Claude Code. It is the first Sonnet-tier model built on the same foundation as the Claude 5 family (alongside Opus 4.8 and the specialized Fable 5 model), and it substantially narrows the capability gap with the top-tier Opus model while remaining priced as a mid-tier workhorse.

---

## Specs

| Spec | Value |
|---|---|
| Context window | **1,000,000 tokens** (up from 200K in the Claude 4 generation) |
| Max output | 128K tokens |
| Vision | High-resolution, up to 2576px |
| Thinking | Adaptive thinking enabled by default, with an `xhigh` effort setting |
| Model ID | `claude-sonnet-5` |

The jump to a 1M-token context window is the largest single increase since Claude 2.1 introduced 200K in late 2023 — Sonnet had been capped at 200K across the entire Claude 3 and 4 generations.

---

## Pricing

Introductory pricing runs through August 31, 2026:

- **$2** / million input tokens
- **$10** / million output tokens
- No long-context premium (a departure from some competing models that surcharge past a context threshold)

After the introductory window, pricing steps up to $3 / million input and $15 / million output.

---

## Benchmarks

Sonnet 5 shows a marked jump over Sonnet 4.6 in agentic performance — reasoning, tool use, coding, and knowledge work:

- **91.1%** on GPQA Diamond
- **71.5%** on the Coding Index
- **53.6%** on SciCode

At its maxed-out `x-high` effort setting, Sonnet 5 performs roughly in line with Opus 4.8 at medium-to-high effort on OSWorld and the agentic-search benchmark BrowseComp — meaning a well-tuned Sonnet 5 request can match Opus-tier results on real-world agentic and browsing tasks at a fraction of the cost.

---

## Features

- Tool use / function calling, with parallel tool calls
- Prompt caching
- Structured outputs via JSON Schema
- Native web search
- Computer use
- Configurable effort levels (including the new `xhigh` tier)

---

## Why It Matters

Sonnet has historically been the "default workhorse" tier — good enough for most tasks, far cheaper than Opus. Sonnet 5 pushes that value proposition further: a 5x larger context window than the prior Sonnet generation, benchmark scores that encroach on Opus 4.8 territory, and no long-context pricing penalty. For agentic coding tools like Claude Code, the 1M context window materially changes what fits in a single session — entire mid-sized codebases can now stay in context without aggressive compaction.

This release is documented in more general terms on the [Claude Model History](claude-model-history) page; this page tracks Sonnet 5 specifically as the current default model referenced throughout this wiki.
